newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma agency ends hearing without SBC ruling.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma agency ends hearing without SBC ruling.

text.p: Oklahoma regulators ended a hearing Wednesday without issuing a ruling on whether SBC Communications Inc should be allowed to offer long-distance phone service from the state.

The three-member Oklahoma Corporation Commission will debate the matter among themselves at a public meeting on Friday, an OCC spokesman told Reuters by phone from Oklahoma City. They could issue a ruling then.

At Wednesday's hearing, the OCC heard an appeal by SBC that it should be allowed to enter the $80 billion long-distance business. Last week, an Oklahoma administrative law judge recommended that the carrier's request be rejected because SBC had not met a federal checklist for entry.
Any decision by the OCC will be forwarded to the Federal Communications Commission, which has final say in the matter.
AT&T Corp, Sprint Corp, Brooks Fiber Properties Inc and Oklahoma's attorney general, among others, told the OCC at Wednesday's hearing that SBC's application was premature and should not be accepted.
